</section><section data-mw-section-id="12" id="mwBn0" aria-labelledby="Libraries"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Libraries">Libraries</h2></div>
<p id="mwBn4">Python's large standard library<sup about="#mwt567" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-86_131-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-86"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-86-131" id="mwBn8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBoA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoE">[</span>123<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoI">]</span></span></a></sup> is commonly cited as one of its greatest strengths. For Internet-facing applications, many standard formats and protocols such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIME" title="MIME" id="mwBoM">MIME</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP" title="HTTP" id="mwBoQ">HTTP</a> are supported. The language includes modules for creating <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_user_interface" title="Graphical user interface" id="mwBoU">graphical user interfaces</a>, connecting to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relational_database" title="Relational database" id="mwBoY">relational databases</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudorandom_number_generator" title="Pseudorandom number generator" id="mwBoc">generating pseudorandom numbers</a>, arithmetic with arbitrary-precision decimals,<sup about="#mwt568" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-88_127-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-88"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-88-127" id="mwBog"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBok"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoo">[</span>119<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBos">]</span></span></a></sup> manipulating <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_expression" title="Regular expression" id="mwBow">regular expressions</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_testing" title="Unit testing" id="mwBo0">unit testing</a>.</p>

<p id="mwBo4">Some parts of the standard library are covered by specifications—for example, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Server_Gateway_Interface" title="Web Server Gateway Interface" id="mwBo8">Web Server Gateway Interface</a> (WSGI) implementation <code id="mwBpA">wsgiref</code> follows PEP 333<sup about="#mwt569" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-89_132-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-89"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-89-132" id="mwBpE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpM">[</span>124<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpQ">]</span></span></a></sup>—but most parts are specified by their code, internal documentation, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_suite" title="Test suite" id="mwBpU">test suites</a>. However, because most of the standard library is cross-platform Python code, only a few modules must be altered or rewritten for variant implementations.</p>

<p id="mwBpY"><span about="#mwt570" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBpc" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2025"},"2":{"wt":"03"},"3":{"wt":"13"},"post":{"wt":","}},"i":0}}]}'>As of 13</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt570"> </span><span about="#mwt570">March</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt570"> </span><span about="#mwt570">2025</span><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt570"></span><span about="#mwt570">,</span><sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;" about="#mwt570"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Python_(programming_language)&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Python_(programming_language)&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt570"></span><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_March_2025" about="#mwt570"/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements" about="#mwt570" id="mwBpg"/> the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_Package_Index" title="Python Package Index" id="mwBpk">Python Package Index</a> (PyPI), the official repository for third-party Python software, contains over 614,339<sup about="#mwt573" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-PyPI_133-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"PyPI"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-PyPI-133"}}'><a href="#cite_note-PyPI-133" id="mwBpo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBps"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpw">[</span>125<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBp0">]</span></span></a></sup> packages.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="13" id="mwBp4" aria-labelledby="Development_environments"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Development_environments">Development environments</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt574" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBp8" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"See also","href":"./Template:See_also"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Comparison of integrated development environments#Python"}},"i":0}}]}'><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt575" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw='{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}'/></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt574" id="mwBqA">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_integrated_development_environments#Python" title="Comparison of integrated development environments">Comparison of integrated development environments §<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>Python</a></div>

<p id="mwBqE">Most<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_specifically_marked_weasel-worded_phrases" about="#mwt576" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBqI" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"which?","href":"./Template:Which%3F"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"August 2025"}},"i":0}}]}'/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_specifically_marked_weasel-worded_phrases_from_August_2025" about="#mwt576"/><sup class="noprint Inline-Template " style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt576" id="mwBqM"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid_weasel_words" title="Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words" class="mw-redirect"><span title="The material near this tag possibly uses too vague attribution or weasel words. (August 2025)">which?</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> Python implementations (including CPython) include a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read–eval–print_loop" title="Read–eval–print loop" id="mwBqQ">read–eval–print loop</a> (REPL); this permits the environment to function as a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_line_interpreter" title="Command line interpreter" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBqU">command line interpreter</a>, with which users enter statements sequentially and receive results immediately.<sup about="#mwt579" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-134" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-134"}}'><a href="#cite_note-134" id="mwBqY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqg">[</span>126<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBqo">Also, CPython is bundled with an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_development_environment" title="Integrated development environment" id="mwBqs">integrated development environment (IDE)</a> called <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDLE" title="IDLE" id="mwBqw">IDLE</a>,<sup about="#mwt584" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-idle_135-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"idle"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-idle-135"}}'><a href="#cite_note-idle-135" id="mwBq0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBq4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBq8">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrA">]</span></span></a></sup> which is oriented toward beginners.<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt580" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBrE" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"cn","href":"./Template:Cn"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"August 2025"}},"i":0}}]}'/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_August_2025" about="#mwt580"/><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt580" id="mwBrI"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (August 2025)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_specifically_marked_weasel-worded_phrases_from_May_2026" about="#mwt581" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBrM" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"by whom?","href":"./Template:By_whom%3F"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"May 2026"}},"i":0}}]}'/><sup class="noprint Inline-Template " style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt581" id="mwBrQ"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch"><span title="The material near this tag may use weasel words or too-vague attribution. (May 2026)">by whom?</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup></p>

<p id="mwBrU">Other shells, including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDLE" title="IDLE" id="mwBrY">IDLE</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPython" title="IPython" id="mwBrc">IPython</a>, add additional capabilities such as improved auto-completion, session-state retention, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syntax_highlighting" title="Syntax highlighting" id="mwBrg">syntax highlighting</a>.<sup about="#mwt585" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-idle_135-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"idle"}}'><a href="#cite_note-idle-135" id="mwBrk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBro"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrs">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt588" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-136" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-136"}}'><a href="#cite_note-136" id="mwBr0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBr4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBr8">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBsE">Standard desktop IDEs include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyCharm" title="PyCharm" id="mwBsI">PyCharm</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spyder_(software)" title="Spyder (software)" id="mwBsM">Spyder</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Studio_Code" title="Visual Studio Code" id="mwBsQ">Visual Studio Code</a>;<sup about="#mwt591" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-137" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-137"}}'><a href="#cite_note-137" id="mwBsU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBsY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsc">[</span>129<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsg">]</span></span></a></sup> there are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser" title="Web browser" id="mwBsk">web browser</a>-based IDEs, such as the following environments:</p>

<ul id="mwBso"><li id="mwBss"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Jupyter" title="Project Jupyter" id="mwBsw">Jupyter Notebooks</a>, an open-source interactive computing platform;<sup about="#mwt594" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-138" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-138"}}'><a href="#cite_note-138" id="mwBs0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBs4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBs8">[</span>130<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtA">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwBtE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PythonAnywhere" title="PythonAnywhere" id="mwBtI">PythonAnywhere</a>, a browser-based IDE and hosting environment; and</li>
<li id="mwBtM">Canopy, a commercial IDE from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enthought" title="Enthought" id="mwBtQ">Enthought</a> that emphasizes <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_computing" title="Scientific computing" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBtU">scientific computing</a>.<sup about="#mwt597" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-139" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-139"}}'><a href="#cite_note-139" id="mwBtY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtg">[</span>131<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt600" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-140" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-140"}}'><a href="#cite_note-140" id="mwBto"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBts"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtw">[</span>132<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt0">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="14" id="mwBt4" aria-labelledby="Implementations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Implementations">Implementations</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt601" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBt8" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"See also","href":"./Template:See_also"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"List of Python software#Python implementations"}},"i":0}}]}'><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt602" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw='{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}'/></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt601" id="mwBuA">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Python_software#Python_implementations" title="List of Python software">List of Python software §<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>Python implementations</a></div>

<section data-mw-section-id="15" id="mwBuE" aria-labelledby="Reference_implementation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Reference_implementation">Reference implementation</h3></div>
<p id="mwBuI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPython" title="CPython" id="mwBuM">CPython</a> is the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reference_implementation" title="Reference implementation" id="mwBuQ">reference implementation</a> of Python. This implementation is written in C; meeting the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C11_(C_standard_revision)" title="C11 (C standard revision)" id="mwBuU">C11</a> standard<sup about="#mwt605" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-141" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-141"}}'><a href="#cite_note-141" id="mwBuY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBug">[</span>133<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuk">]</span></span></a></sup> since version 3.11. Older versions use the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C89_(C_version)" title="C89 (C version)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBuo">C89</a> standard with several select <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C99" title="C99" id="mwBus">C99</a> features, but third-party extensions are not limited to older C versions—e.g., they can be implemented using C11 or C++.<sup about="#mwt608" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-142" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-142"}}'><a href="#cite_note-142" id="mwBuw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBu0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBu4">[</span>134<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBu8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt609" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-66_143-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-66"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-66-143" id="mwBvA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvI">[</span>135<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvM">]</span></span></a></sup> CPython <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler" title="Compiler" id="mwBvQ">compiles</a> Python programs into an intermediate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bytecode" title="Bytecode" id="mwBvU">bytecode</a>,<sup about="#mwt610" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-67_144-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-67"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-67-144" id="mwBvY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvg">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvk">]</span></span></a></sup> which is then executed by a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_machine" title="Virtual machine" id="mwBvo">virtual machine</a>.<sup about="#mwt611" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-68_145-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-68"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-68-145" id="mwBvs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBv0">[</span>137<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBv4">]</span></span></a></sup> CPython is distributed with a large standard library written in a combination of C and native Python.</p>

<p id="mwBv8">CPython is available for many platforms, including Windows and most modern <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix-like" title="Unix-like" id="mwBwA">Unix-like</a> systems, including macOS (and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_M1" title="Apple M1" id="mwBwE">Apple M1</a> Macs, since Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBwI"> </span>3.9.1, using an experimental installer). <!-- "Windows Vista support dropped in Python 3.7" -->Starting with Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBwM"> </span>3.9, the Python installer intentionally fails to install on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_7" title="Windows 7" id="mwBwQ">Windows 7</a> and 8<!-- but not 8.1? -->;<sup about="#mwt614" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-146" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-146"}}'><a href="#cite_note-146" id="mwBwU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBwY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwc">[</span>138<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt617" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-147" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-147"}}'><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_XP" title="Windows XP" id="mwBw0">Windows XP</a> was supported until Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBw4"> </span>3.5.<!--"Windows XP support dropped in Python 3.5"--> Old Python versions unofficially support <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenVMS" title="OpenVMS" id="mwBw8">VMS</a> (mostly supporting<sup href="#cite_note-148" id="mwBxA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxI">[</span>140<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxM">]</span></span></a></sup>) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenVMS" title="OpenVMS" id="mwBxQ">OpenVMS</a> x86-64 has Python 3.10 support.<sup about="#mwt623" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-149" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-149"}}'><a href="#cite_note-149" id="mwBxU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxc">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxg">]</span></span></a></sup><!--"Put online a new version of Python 3.10.0a (IA64only)"--><sup portability was one of Python's earliest priorities.<sup about="#mwt627" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-69_151-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-69"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-69-151" id="mwBx0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBx4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBx8">[</span>143<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwByA">]</span></span></a></sup> During development of Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwByE"> </span>1 and 2, even <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS/2" title="OS/2" id="mwByI">OS/2</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solaris_(operating_system)" title="Solaris (operating system)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwByM">Solaris</a> were supported;<!-- Also python&#x2D;3.2.2 at http://unixpackages.com/packages/package&#x2D;list --><sup about="#mwt630" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DownloadOther_9-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"DownloadOther"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-DownloadOther-9"}}'><a <p id="mwByg">All current Python versions (since 3.7) support only operating systems that feature multithreading<!-- (then in 3.7 removing support for [[IRIX]]; and before many other operating systems such as [[OS/2]] and [[OpenVMS|VMS]]) -->, by now supporting not nearly as many operating systems (dropping many outdated) than in the past.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="16" id="mwByk" aria-labelledby="Limitations_of_the_reference_implementation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Limitations_of_the_reference_implementation">Limitations of the reference implementation</h3></div>
<ul id="mwByo"><li id="mwBys">The energy usage of Python with CPython for typically written code is much worse than C by a factor of 75.88.<sup about="#mwt633" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_152-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:1-152"}}'><a href="#cite_note-:1-152" id="mwByw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBy0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBy4">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBy8">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwBzA">The throughput of Python with CPython for typically written code is worse than C by a factor of 71.9.<sup about="#mwt634" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_152-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-:1-152" id="mwBzE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzM">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzQ">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwBzU">The average memory usage of CPython for typically written code is worse than C by a factor of 2.4.<sup about="#mwt635" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_152-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-:1-152" id="mwBzY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzg">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzk">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="17" id="mwBzo" aria-labelledby="Other_implementations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Other_implementations">Other implementations</h3></div>
<p id="mwBzs">All alternative implementations have at least slightly different semantics. For example, an alternative may include unordered dictionaries<!-- like with Codon; also PyPy? Cython? -->, in contrast to other current Python versions. As another example in the larger Python ecosystem, PyPy does not support the full C Python API.</p>

<p id="mwBzw">Creating an executable with Python often is done by bundling an entire Python interpreter into the executable, which causes binary sizes to be massive for small programs,<sup about="#mwt638" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-153" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-153"}}'><a href="#cite_note-153" id="mwBz0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBz4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBz8">[</span>145<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0A">]</span></span></a></sup> yet there exist implementations that are capable of truly compiling Python. Alternative implementations include the following:</p>

<ul id="mwB0E"><li id="mwB0I"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyPy" title="PyPy" id="mwB0M">PyPy</a> is a faster, compliant interpreter of Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB0Q"> </span>2.7 and <!-- 3.8 (both are outdated CPython versions) --> 3.11.<sup about="#mwt639" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-70_154-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-70"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-70-154" id="mwB0U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0c">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0g">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt642" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-155" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-155"}}'><a href="#cite_note-155" id="mwB0k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0s">[</span>147<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0w">]</span></span></a></sup> PyPy's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just-in-time_compiler" title="Just-in-time compiler" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB00">just-in-time compiler</a> often improves speed significantly relative to CPython, but PyPy does not support some libraries written in C.<sup about="#mwt643" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-71_156-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-71"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-71-156" id="mwB04"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB08"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1A">[</span>148<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1E">]</span></span></a></sup> PyPy offers support for the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RISC-V" title="RISC-V" id="mwB1I">RISC-V</a> instruction-set architecture.</li>
<li id="mwB1M">Codon is an implementation with an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahead-of-time_compilation" title="Ahead-of-time compilation" id="mwB1Q">ahead-of-time (AOT) compiler</a>, which compiles a statically-typed Python-like language whose "syntax and semantics are nearly identical to Python's, there are some notable differences"<sup about="#mwt646" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-157" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-157"}}'><a href="#cite_note-157" id="mwB1U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB1Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1c">[</span>149<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1g">]</span></span></a></sup> For example, Codon uses 64-bit machine integers for speed, not arbitrarily as with Python; Codon developers claim that speedups over CPython are usually on the order of ten to a hundred times. Codon compiles to machine code (via <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLVM" title="LLVM" id="mwB1k">LLVM</a>) and supports native multithreading.<sup about="#mwt649" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-158" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-158"}}'><a href="#cite_note-158" id="mwB1o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB1s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1w">[</span>150<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB10">]</span></span></a></sup> <!-- It's compile has a restrictive BSL licence, but it doesn't affect generated code: --> Codon can also compile to Python extension modules that can be imported and used from Python.</li>
<li id="mwB14"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MicroPython" title="MicroPython" id="mwB18">MicroPython</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CircuitPython" title="CircuitPython" id="mwB2A">CircuitPython</a> are Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB2E"> </span>3 variants that are optimized for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcontroller" title="Microcontroller" id="mwB2I">microcontrollers</a>, including the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego_Mindstorms_EV3" title="Lego Mindstorms EV3" id="mwB2M">Lego Mindstorms EV3</a>.<sup about="#mwt652" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-159" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-159"}}'><a href="#cite_note-159" id="mwB2Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2Y">[</span>151<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2c">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwB2g">Pyston is a variant of the Python runtime that uses just-in-time compilation to speed up execution of Python programs.<sup about="#mwt655" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-160" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-160"}}'><a href="#cite_note-160" id="mwB2k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2s">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2w">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwB20">Cinder is a performance-oriented fork of CPython 3.8 that features a number of optimizations, including bytecode inline caching, eager evaluation of coroutines, a method-at-a-time <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just-in-time_compilation" title="Just-in-time compilation" id="mwB24">JIT</a>, and an experimental bytecode compiler.<sup about="#mwt658" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-161" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-161"}}'><a href="#cite_note-161" id="mwB28"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3E">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3I">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwB3M">The Snek<!-- (previously named Newt) --><sup about="#mwt661" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-162" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-162"}}'><a href="#cite_note-162" id="mwB3Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3Y">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3c">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt664" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-163" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-163"}}'><a href="#cite_note-163" id="mwB3g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3o">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3s">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt667" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-164" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-164"}}'><a href="#cite_note-164" id="mwB3w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB30"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB34">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB38">]</span></span></a></sup><!-- https://keithp.com/blogs/newt&#x2D;lola/ https://bipes.net.br/snek&#x2D;web&#x2D;uploader/ --> embedded computing language "is Python-inspired, but it is not Python. It is possible to write Snek programs that run under a full Python system, but most Python programs will not run under Snek."<sup about="#mwt670" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-165" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-165"}}'><a href="#cite_note-165" id="mwB4A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4I">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4M">]</span></span></a></sup> Snek is compatible with 8-bit <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AVR_microcontrollers" title="AVR microcontrollers" id="mwB4Q">AVR microcontrollers</a> such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATmega" title="ATmega" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB4U">ATmega 328P</a>-based Arduino, as well as larger microcontrollers that are compatible with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MicroPython" title="MicroPython" id="mwB4Y">MicroPython</a>. Snek is an imperative language that (unlike Python) omits <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object-oriented_programming" title="Object-oriented programming" id="mwB4c">object-oriented programming</a>. Snek supports only one numeric data type, which features 32-bit <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_precision" title="Single precision" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB4g">single precision</a> (resembling <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript" title="JavaScript" id="mwB4k">JavaScript</a> numbers, though smaller).<!-- "Snek is a tiny embeddable language targeting processors with only a few kB of flash and ram. Think of something that would have been running BASIC years ago and you'll have the idea. These processors are too small to run MicroPython." "Snekboard is a custom embedded computer designed to run Snek or CircuitPython." --></li>
<li id="mwB4o">RustPython is an implementation written in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)" title="Rust (programming language)" id="mwB4s">Rust</a> language. It aims to be compatible with CPython, including its C-ABI.<sup about="#mwt673" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-166" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-166"}}'><a href="#cite_note-166" id="mwB4w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB40"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB44">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB48">]</span></span></a></sup> Currently, it is used in <a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://www.greptime.com/product/db" class="external text" id="mwB5A">GrepTimeDB</a> and <a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://astral.sh/ruff" class="external text" id="mwB5E">Ruff</a> among other projects.</li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="18" id="mwB5I" aria-labelledby="Unsupported_implementations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Unsupported_implementations">Unsupported implementations</h3></div>
<p id="mwB5M"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stackless_Python" title="Stackless Python" id="mwB5Q">Stackless Python</a> is a significant fork of CPython that implements <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microthread" title="Microthread" id="mwB5U">microthreads</a>. This implementation uses the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_stack" title="Call stack" id="mwB5Y">call stack</a> differently, thus allowing massively concurrent programs. PyPy also offers a stackless version.<sup about="#mwt674" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-73_167-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-73"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-73-167" id="mwB5c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB5g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5k">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5o">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB5s">Just-in-time Python compilers have been developed, but are now unsupported:</p>
<ul id="mwB5w"><li id="mwB50">Google began a project named <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unladen_Swallow" title="Unladen Swallow" id="mwB54">Unladen Swallow</a> in 2009: this project aimed to speed up the Python interpreter five-fold by using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLVM" title="LLVM" id="mwB58">LLVM</a>, and improve <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multithreading_(computer_architecture)" title="Multithreading (computer architecture)" id="mwB6A">multithreading</a> capability for scaling to thousands of cores,<sup about="#mwt675" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-74_168-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-74"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-74-168" id="mwB6E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6M">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6Q">]</span></span></a></sup> while typical implementations are limited by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_interpreter_lock" title="Global interpreter lock" id="mwB6U">global interpreter lock</a>.</li>
<li id="mwB6Y"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psyco" title="Psyco" id="mwB6c">Psyco</a> is a discontinued <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just-in-time_compilation" title="Just-in-time compilation" id="mwB6g">just-in-time</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run-time_algorithm_specialization" title="Run-time algorithm specialization" id="mwB6k">specializing</a> compiler, which integrates with CPython and transforms bytecode to machine code at runtime. The emitted code is specialized for certain <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_type" title="Data type" id="mwB6o">data types</a> and is faster than standard Python code. Psyco does not support Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB6s"> </span>2.7 or later.</li>
<li id="mwB6w"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyS60" title="PyS60" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB60">PyS60</a> was a Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB64"> </span>2 interpreter for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_60" title="Series 60" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB68">Series 60</a> mobile phones, which was released by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia" title="Nokia" id="mwB7A">Nokia</a> in 2005. The interpreter implemented many modules from Python's standard library, as well as additional modules for integration with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbian" title="Symbian" id="mwB7E">Symbian</a> operating system. The Nokia <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N900" title="N900" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB7I">N900</a> also supports Python through the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTK" title="GTK" id="mwB7M">GTK</a> widget library, allowing programs to be written and run on the target device.<sup about="#mwt678" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-169" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-169"}}'><a href="#cite_note-169" id="mwB7Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB7U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7Y">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7c">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="19" id="mwB7g" aria-labelledby="Transpilers_to_other_languages"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Transpilers_to_other_languages">Transpilers to other languages</h3></div>
<p id="mwB7k">There are several compilers/<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transpiler" title="Transpiler" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB7o">transpilers</a> to high-level object languages; the source language is unrestricted Python, a subset of Python, or a language similar to Python:</p>
<ul id="mwB7s"><li id="mwB7w">Brython<sup about="#mwt681" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-170" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-170"}}'><a href="#cite_note-170" id="mwB70"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB74"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB78">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8A">]</span></span></a></sup> and Transcrypt<sup about="#mwt684" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-171" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-171"}}'><a href="#cite_note-171" id="mwB8E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB8I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8M">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8Q">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt687" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-172" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-172"}}'><a href="#cite_note-172" id="mwB8U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB8Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8c">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8g">]</span></span></a></sup> compile Python to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript" title="JavaScript" id="mwB8k">JavaScript</a>.</li>
<li id="mwB8o"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cython" title="Cython" id="mwB8s">Cython</a> compiles a superset of Python<!-- actually 2.7 by default, but Python 3 by override --> to C. The resulting code can be used with Python via direct C-level API calls into the Python interpreter.</li>
<li id="mwB8w">PyJL compiles/transpiles a subset of Python to "human-readable, maintainable, and high-performance Julia source code".<sup about="#mwt690" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-PyJL_78-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"PyJL"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-PyJL-78"}}'><a href="#cite_note-PyJL-78" id="mwB80"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB84"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB88">[</span>75<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9A">]</span></span></a></sup> Despite the developers' performance claims, this is not possible for <i id="mwB9E">arbitrary</i> Python code; that is, compiling to a faster language or machine code is known to be impossible in the general case. The semantics of Python might potentially be changed, but in many cases speedup is possible with few or no changes in the Python code. The faster Julia source code can then be used from Python or compiled to machine code.</li>
<li id="mwB9I"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuitka" title="Nuitka" id="mwB9M">Nuitka</a> compiles Python into C<!-- "is the optimizing Python compiler written in Python that creates executables that run without a separate installer"-->.<sup about="#mwt693" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-173" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-173"}}'><a href="#cite_note-173" id="mwB9Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9Y">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9c">]</span></span></a></sup> This compiler works with Python 3.4 to 3.13 (and 2.6 and 2.7) for Python's main supported platforms (and Windows 7 or even Windows XP) and for Android. The compiler developers claim full support for Python 3.10, <!-- "also finishes full compatibility with the match statements of 3.10"  "From here on, we need to re&#x2D;visit compatibility. A few more obscured 3.10 features are missing, the 3.11 compatibility is not yet complete" -->partial support for Python 3.11 and 3.12, <!-- "This release bumps the long&#x2D;awaited 3.12 support to a complete level. Now, Nuitka behaves identically to CPython 3.12 for the most part. .. After being late with 3.12 support, we will now be early with 3.13 support if all goes well." --> and experimental support for Python 3.13. Nuitka supports macOS including Apple Silicon-based versions. <!-- "While arm64 (M1) only builds and x86_64 (Intel) only builds work, the value universal which of course implies twice the size, and as such has other disadvantages, is not yet supported. --> The compiler is free of cost, though it has commercial add-ons (e.g., for hiding source code).<!-- "Container Builds (public + commercial)" --></li>
<li id="mwB9g"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numba" title="Numba" id="mwB9k">Numba</a> is a JIT compiler that is used from Python; the compiler translates a subset of Python and NumPy code into fast machine code. This tool is enabled by adding a decorator to the relevant Python code.</li>
<li id="mwB9o">Pythran compiles a subset of Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB9s"> </span>3 to C++ (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++11" title="C++11" id="mwB9w">C++11</a>).<sup about="#mwt696" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Guelton_Brunet_Amini_Merlini_2015_p=014001_174-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Guelton Brunet Amini Merlini 2015 p=014001"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Guelton_Brunet_Amini_Merlini_2015_p=014001-174"}}'><a href="#cite_note-Guelton_Brunet_Amini_Merlini_2015_p=014001-174" id="mwB90"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB94"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB98">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-A">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwB-E"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RPython" title="RPython" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB-I">RPython</a> can be compiled to C, and it is used to build the PyPy interpreter for Python.</li>
<li id="mwB-M">The Python → 11l → C++ transpiler<sup about="#mwt699" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-175" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-175"}}'><a href="#cite_note-175" id="mwB-Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB-U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-Y">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-c">]</span></span></a></sup> compiles a subset of Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB-g"> </span>3 to C++ (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++17" title="C++17" id="mwB-k">C++17</a>).</li></ul>

<p id="mwB-o">There are also specialized compilers:</p>
<ul id="mwB-s"><li id="mwB-w"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MyHDL" title="MyHDL" id="mwB-0">MyHDL</a> is a Python-based <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardware_description_language" title="Hardware description language" id="mwB-4">hardware description language</a> (HDL) that converts MyHDL code to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verilog" title="Verilog" id="mwB-8">Verilog</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VHDL" title="VHDL" id="mwB_A">VHDL</a> code.</li></ul>

<p id="mwB_E">Some older projects existed, as well as compilers not designed for use with Python 3.x and related syntax:</p>
<ul id="mwB_I"><li id="mwB_M">Google's Grumpy <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transpile" title="Transpile" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB_Q">transpiles</a> Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwB_U"> </span>2 to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language)" title="Go (programming language)" id="mwB_Y">Go</a>.<sup about="#mwt702" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-176" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-176"}}'><a href="#cite_note-176" id="mwB_c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB_g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_k">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_o">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt705" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-177" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-177"}}'><a href="#cite_note-177" id="mwB_s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB_w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_0">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_4">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt708" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-178" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-178"}}'><a href="#cite_note-178" id="mwB_8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAE">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAI">]</span></span></a></sup> The latest release was in 2017.</li>
<li id="mwCAM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IronPython" title="IronPython" id="mwCAQ">IronPython</a><!-- (abandoned by Microsoft) --> allows running Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCAU"> </span>2.7 programs with the .NET <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Language_Runtime" title="Common Language Runtime" id="mwCAY">Common Language Runtime</a>.<sup about="#mwt711" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-179" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-179"}}'><a href="#cite_note-179" id="mwCAc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAk">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAo">]</span></span></a></sup> An <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle#Alpha" title="Software release life cycle" id="mwCAs">alpha</a> version (released in 2021), is available for "Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCAw"> </span>3.4, although features and behaviors from later versions may be included."<sup about="#mwt714" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-180" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-180"}}'><a href="#cite_note-180" id="mwCA0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCA4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCA8">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBA">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCBE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jython" title="Jython" id="mwCBI">Jython</a> compiles Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCBM"> </span>2.7 to Java bytecode, allowing the use of Java libraries from a Python program.<sup about="#mwt717" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-181" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-181"}}'><a href="#cite_note-181" id="mwCBQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCBU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBY">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBc">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCBg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrex_(programming_language)" title="Pyrex (programming language)" id="mwCBk">Pyrex</a> (last released in 2010) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shed_Skin" title="Shed Skin" id="mwCBo">Shed Skin</a> (last released in 2013) compile to C and C++ respectively.</li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="20" id="mwCBs" aria-labelledby="Performance"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Performance">Performance</h3></div>
<p id="mwCBw">A performance comparison among various Python implementations, using a non-numerical (combinatorial) workload, was presented at EuroSciPy '13.<sup about="#mwt720" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-182" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-182"}}'><a href="#cite_note-182" id="mwCB0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCB4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCB8">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCA">]</span></span></a></sup> In addition, Python's performance relative to other programming languages is benchmarked by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Computer_Language_Benchmarks_Game" title="The Computer Language Benchmarks Game" id="mwCCE">The Computer Language Benchmarks Game</a>.<sup about="#mwt723" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-183" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-183"}}'><a href="#cite_note-183" id="mwCCI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCCM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCQ">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCCY">There are several approaches to optimizing Python performance, despite the inherent slowness of an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpreted_language" title="Interpreted language" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCCc">interpreted language</a>. These approaches include the following strategies or tools:</p>

<ul id="mwCCg"><li id="mwCCk"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just-in-time_compilation" title="Just-in-time compilation" id="mwCCo">Just-in-time compilation</a>: Dynamically compiling parts of a Python program during the execution of the program. This technique is used in libraries such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numba" title="Numba" id="mwCCs">Numba</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyPy" title="PyPy" id="mwCCw">PyPy</a>.</li>
<li id="mwCC0"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler" title="Compiler" id="mwCC4">Static compilation</a>: Sometimes, Python code can be compiled into machine code sometime before execution. An example of this approach is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cython" title="Cython" id="mwCC8">Cython</a>, which compiles Python into C.</li>
<li id="mwCDA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_computing" title="Concurrent computing" id="mwCDE">Concurrency</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_computing" title="Parallel computing" id="mwCDI">parallelism</a>: Multiple tasks can be run simultaneously. Python contains modules such as `multiprocessing` to support this form of parallelism. Moreover, this approach helps to overcome limitations of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Interpreter_Lock" title="Global Interpreter Lock" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCDM">Global Interpreter Lock</a> (GIL) in CPU tasks.</li>
<li id="mwCDQ">Efficient <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_structures" title="Data structures" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCDU">data structures</a>: Performance can also be improved by using data types such as <code id="mwCDY">Set</code> for membership tests, or <code id="mwCDc">deque</code> from <code id="mwCDg">collections</code> for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queueing_theory" title="Queueing theory" id="mwCDk">queue</a> operations.</li>
<li id="mwCDo">Performance gains can be observed by utilizing libraries such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NumPy" title="NumPy" id="mwCDs">NumPy</a>. Most high performance Python libraries use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language)" title="C (programming language)" id="mwCDw">C</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortran" title="Fortran" id="mwCD0">Fortran</a> under the hood instead of the Python interpreter.<sup about="#mwt726" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-184" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-184"}}'><a href="#cite_note-184" id="mwCD4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCD8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEA">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEE">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="21" id="mwCEI" aria-labelledby="Language_development"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Language_development">Language development</h2></div>
<p id="mwCEM">Python's development is conducted mostly through the <i id="mwCEQ">Python Enhancement Proposal</i> (PEP) process; this process is the primary mechanism for proposing major new features, collecting community input on issues, and documenting Python design decisions.<sup about="#mwt727" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-PepCite000_185-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"PepCite000"}}'><a href="#cite_note-PepCite000-185" id="mwCEU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCEY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEc">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEg">]</span></span></a></sup> Python coding style is covered in PEP<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCEk"> </span>8.<sup about="#mwt728" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-pep8_93-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"pep8"}}'><a href="#cite_note-pep8-93" id="mwCEo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCEs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEw">[</span>86<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCE0">]</span></span></a></sup> Outstanding PEPs are reviewed and commented on by the Python community and the steering council.<sup about="#mwt729" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-PepCite000_185-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"PepCite000"}}'><a href="#cite_note-PepCite000-185" id="mwCE4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCE8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFA">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCFI">Enhancement of the language corresponds with development of the CPython reference implementation. The mailing list python-dev is the primary forum for the language's development. Specific issues were originally discussed in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundup_(issue_tracker)" title="Roundup (issue tracker)" id="mwCFM">Roundup</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bug_tracker" title="Bug tracker" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCFQ">bug tracker</a> hosted by the foundation.<sup about="#mwt730" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-21_186-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-21"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-21-186" id="mwCFU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFc">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFg">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2022, all issues and discussions were migrated to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub" title="GitHub" id="mwCFk">GitHub</a>.<sup about="#mwt733" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-187" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-187"}}'><a href="#cite_note-187" id="mwCFo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFw">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCF0">]</span></span></a></sup> Development originally took place on a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-hosting_(web_services)" title="Self-hosting (web services)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCF4">self-hosted</a> source-code repository running <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercurial" title="Mercurial" id="mwCF8">Mercurial</a>, until Python moved to GitHub in January 2017.<sup about="#mwt736" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-py_dev_guide_188-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"py_dev_guide"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-py_dev_guide-188"}}'><a href="#cite_note-py_dev_guide-188" id="mwCGA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGI">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCGQ">CPython's public releases have three types, distinguished by which part of the version number is incremented:</p>
<ul id="mwCGU"><li id="mwCGY"><i id="mwCGc">Backward-incompatible versions</i>, where code is expected to break and must be manually <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ported" title="Ported" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCGg">ported</a>. The first part of the version number is incremented. These releases happen infrequently—version 3.0 was released 8 years after 2.0. According to Guido van Rossum, a version 4.0 will probably never exist.<sup about="#mwt739" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-189" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-189"}}'><a href="#cite_note-189" id="mwCGk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGs">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGw">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCG0"><i id="mwCG4">Major or "feature" releases</i> are largely compatible with the previous version but introduce new features. The second part of the version number is incremented. Starting with Python<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCG8"> </span>3.9, these releases are expected to occur annually.<sup about="#mwt742" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-190" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-190"}}'><a href="#cite_note-190" id="mwCHA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHI">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt745" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-191" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-191"}}'><a href="#cite_note-191" id="mwCHQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHY">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHc">]</span></span></a></sup> Each major version is supported by bug fixes for several years after its release.<sup about="#mwt746" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-release-schedule_192-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"release-schedule"}}'><a href="#cite_note-release-schedule-192" id="mwCHg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHo">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHs">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCHw"><i id="mwCH0">Bug fix releases</i>,<sup about="#mwt747" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-22_193-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-22"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-22-193" id="mwCH4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCH8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIA">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIE">]</span></span></a></sup> which introduce no new features, occur approximately every three months; these releases are made when a sufficient number of bugs have been fixed <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream_(software_development)" title="Upstream (software development)" id="mwCII">upstream</a> since the last release. Security vulnerabilities are also patched in these releases. The third and final part of the version number is incremented.<sup about="#mwt748" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-22_193-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-22"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-22-193" id="mwCIM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCIQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIU">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIY">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

<p id="mwCIc">Many <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_release" title="Beta release" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCIg">alpha, beta, and release-candidates</a> are also released as previews and for testing before final releases. Although there is a rough schedule for releases, they are often delayed if the code is not ready yet. Python's development team monitors the state of the code by running a large <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_test" title="Unit test" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCIk">unit test</a> suite during development.<sup about="#mwt749" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-23_194-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-23"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-23-194" id="mwCIo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCIs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIw">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCI0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCI4">The major <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_conference" title="Academic conference" id="mwCI8">academic conference</a> on Python is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyCon" title="PyCon" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCJA">PyCon</a>. Also, there are special Python mentoring programs, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyLadies" title="PyLadies" id="mwCJE">PyLadies</a>.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="22" id="mwCJI" aria-labelledby="Naming"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Naming">Naming</h2></div>
<p id="mwCJM">Python's name is inspired by the British comedy group <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Python" title="Monty Python" id="mwCJQ">Monty Python</a>, whom Python creator Guido van Rossum enjoyed while developing the language. Monty Python references appear frequently in Python code and culture;<sup about="#mwt753" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-tutorial-chapter1_195-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"tutorial-chapter1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-tutorial-chapter1-195" id="mwCJU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCJY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJc">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJg">]</span></span></a></sup> for example, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metasyntactic_variable" title="Metasyntactic variable" id="mwCJk">metasyntactic variables</a> often used in Python literature are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spam_(Monty_Python_sketch)" title="Spam (Monty Python sketch)" id="mwCJo"><i id="mwCJs">spam</i> and <i id="mwCJw">eggs</i></a>, rather than the traditional <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foobar" title="Foobar" id="mwCJ0"><i id="mwCJ4">foo</i> and <i id="mwCJ8">bar</i></a>.<sup about="#mwt754" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-tutorial-chapter1_195-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"tutorial-chapter1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-tutorial-chapter1-195" id="mwCKA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKI">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt755" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AutoNT-26_196-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AutoNT-26"}}'><a href="#cite_note-AutoNT-26-196" id="mwCKQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKY">[</span>188<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKc">]</span></span></a></sup> Also, the official Python documentation contains various references to Monty Python routines.<sup about="#mwt750" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELutz201317_197-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"group":"","name":"FOOTNOTELutz201317"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELutz201317-197"},"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"sfn","href":"./Template:Sfn"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Lutz"},"2":{"wt":"2013"},"p":{"wt":"17"}},"i":0}}]}'><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELutz201317-197" id="mwCKg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKo">[</span>189<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt758" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-198" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-198"}}'><a href="#cite_note-198" id="mwCKw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCK0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCK4">[</span>190<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCK8">]</span></span></a></sup> Python users are sometimes referred to as "Pythonistas".<sup about="#mwt761" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-introducing_python_199-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"introducing_python"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-introducing_python-199"}}'><a href="#cite_note-introducing_python-199" id="mwCLA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLI">[</span>191<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="23" id="mwCLQ" aria-labelledby="Languages_influenced_by_Python"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Languages_influenced_by_Python">Languages influenced by Python</h2></div>
<ul id="mwCLU"><li id="mwCLY"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobra_(programming_language)" title="Cobra (programming language)" id="mwCLc">Cobra</a> has an <i id="mwCLg">Acknowledgements</i> document that lists Python first among influencing languages.<sup about="#mwt764" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-200" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-200"}}'><a href="#cite_note-200" id="mwCLk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLs">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLw">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCL0"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECMAScript" title="ECMAScript" id="mwCL4">ECMAScript</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript" title="JavaScript" id="mwCL8">JavaScript</a> borrowed iterators and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generator_(computer_science)" title="Generator (computer science)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCMA">generators</a> from Python.<sup about="#mwt767" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-201" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-201"}}'><a href="#cite_note-201" id="mwCME"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMM">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMQ">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCMU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language)" title="Go (programming language)" id="mwCMY">Go</a> is designed for "speed of working in a dynamic language like Python".<sup about="#mwt770" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-202" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-202"}}'><a href="#cite_note-202" id="mwCMc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMk">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMo">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCMs"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_(programming_language)" title="Julia (programming language)" id="mwCMw">Julia</a> was designed to be "as usable for general programming as Python".<sup about="#mwt771" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Julia_35-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Julia"}}'><a href="#cite_note-Julia-35" id="mwCM0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCM4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCM8">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNA">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCNE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojo_(programming_language)" title="Mojo (programming language)" id="mwCNI">Mojo</a> is almost<sup about="#mwt774" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Mojo_36-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Mojo"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Mojo-36"}}'><a href="#cite_note-Mojo-36" id="mwCNM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNU">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNY">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt777" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-203" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-203"}}'><a href="#cite_note-203" id="mwCNc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNk">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNo">]</span></span></a></sup> a superset of Python.<sup about="#mwt780" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-204" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-204"}}'><a href="#cite_note-204" id="mwCNs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCN0">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCN4">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCN8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDScript" title="GDScript" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCOA">GDScript</a> is strongly influenced by Python.<sup about="#mwt783" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-205" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-205"}}'><a href="#cite_note-205" id="mwCOE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCOI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOM">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOQ">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCOU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_Groovy" title="Apache Groovy" id="mwCOY"> Groovy</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boo_(programming_language)" title="Boo (programming language)" id="mwCOc">Boo</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoffeeScript" title="CoffeeScript" id="mwCOg">CoffeeScript</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_Sharp_(programming_language)" title="F Sharp (programming language)" id="mwCOk">F#</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nim_(programming_language)" title="Nim (programming language)" id="mwCOo">Nim</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_(programming_language)" title="Ruby (programming language)" id="mwCOs">Ruby</a>,<sup about="#mwt784" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-bini_37-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"bini"}}'><a href="#cite_note-bini-37" id="mwCOw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCO0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCO4">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCO8">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swift_(programming_language)" title="Swift (programming language)" id="mwCPA">Swift</a>,<sup about="#mwt787" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-lattner2014_38-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"lattner2014"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-lattner2014-38"}}'><a href="#cite_note-lattner2014-38" id="mwCPE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPM">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPQ">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V_(programming_language)" title="V (programming language)" id="mwCPU">V</a><sup about="#mwt790" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-vpeople_39-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"vpeople"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-vpeople-39"}}'><a href="#cite_note-vpeople-39" id="mwCPY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPg">[</span>37<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPk">]</span></span></a></sup> have been influenced, as well.</li></ul>
